`aria-activedescendant` tells a screen reader which child of a widget is active while the focus stays on the widget itself. That only works if the widget can take the focus. A plain `div` cannot, so the attribute does nothing there until you add a `tabIndex` of `0` or `-1`.

Elements that take the focus by themselves, such as `input`, `select` and `button`, need no `tabIndex`. Components are not checked.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
const list = (
  <div role="listbox" aria-activedescendant={activeId}>
    {options}
  </div>
);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
const list = (
  <div role="listbox" tabIndex={0} aria-activedescendant={activeId}>
    {options}
  </div>
);

const grid = <div role="grid" tabIndex={-1} aria-activedescendant={activeId} />;
const search = <input role="combobox" aria-activedescendant={activeId} />;
```
